# truck-driver-ui-screen-feedback

- **callId**: `call-3242a54c-0ff4-4116-ae35-93bb6728343d`
- **started**: 2026-09-19 06:42:56 CDT
- **ended**: 2026-09-19 06:55:48 CDT
- **duration**: 12m 52s (772350 ms)
- **ending**: hung-up
- **model**: grok-voice-3.0
- **agentId**: `fe0b6c3f-adcf-483f-a7f9-335890abd80d`

## Transcript

**user**: So there's three things on this screen. The first one is bright white. There isn't a truck driver out here that wants to deal with this bright white screen at night, or even during the day. Let's switch it over to a parchment color, like Leonardo Da Vinci's parchment. Um, so it it has a I'm not doing it because of aesthetics, I'm doing it because nobody likes white. It's just stupid. Um, we have to turn our tablets dimness way down because of that stupid crap. The second thing is see where it says routes? That is completely worthless. That route box needs to take up the entire space where it says forms. Forms needs to be moved elsewhere. Routes should have the trailer number. Uh, we can pull two trailers at a time, so if it's the same if we're pulling a van or we're pulling two pups, it needs to have the trailer numbers, destination, and origin listed on there. Um, both with our codes, like for instance, um, right now I'm at uh ARL 193, that's Arlington 193. I just left Dallas. Um, Dallas is DAL uh 089. So, for instance, that route should say um uh DAL 089, list the two trailers I'm pulling 'cause I just pulled a set, and then once I go into the system and punch in my uh my dolly, that dolly should show up on that route screen so that I can see it. Once I uh entered all the info information and I I left, I uh dispatched myself on it, on that route screen it needs to be very clear, it's going to be color-coded saying that everything is green. That that routes uh button will turn yellow or red depending on if there's an error. Sometimes we get an error because uh the route um the we have a problem with the trailer, like a trailer hasn't been moved properly, so that would be a yellow. If a um if a piece of equipment is actually showing in the shop and we shouldn't even be pulling it, it should pop up red, that kind of thing.

**assistant**: Parchment it is — white's just glare, and drivers are right to hate it.

**assistant**: On the routes side, I'm picturing that panel showing your two trailer numbers, the dolly once you punch it in, and the DAL-to-ARL codes front and center — green, yellow, or red so you know in a glance whether you're clear to roll or something's wrong with the equipment. You said there were three things — what's the third?

**assistant**: That's all captured — parchment, the fat routes panel with both trailers, the dolly, and the green-yellow-red status. What's the third one?

**user**: Okay, up at the top where it has the O for my That's a hot tap. So unfortunately, whenever we have a message pop up, like we're going back to check and make sure uh we can actually pull the trailer, a message will pop up. Right in that spot, when we're trying to, or so we're trying, it's the arrow to back back out of the screen so we can go back to the messages, and when you're backing out of it, um, the mess the uh the pop-up message disappears, the arrow disappears, and you're still tapping and you then you tap that O. And when you tap that O, it takes you to your info, which is completely worthless. I I don't I already know my info. I why they would put that as a hot spot, I don't know. So basically where it says Olson A September 19th and the truck number, first that truck number needs to be bigger so that the driver knows what he's driving. Um, believe it or not, I mean like me, I drive a different truck practically every day. But uh but that O either needs to have its hot uh hot tap ability removed, or it needs to be moved next to my name and September 19th 'cause it's in completely the wrong spot.

**assistant**: That O is a landmine — you're backing out of a message, it vanishes, and your finger lands on it by accident.

**user**: There's a few other things that I'd like to do, like uh basically um if they don't like the parchment background so that it's not so glaring, I would almost like to do like a a shadow, not shadowed, uh a dim uh branding system. You know, like a a photograph of Estes terminals. Um, something like that where the background actually, the problem with that is it might start causing problems where text will disappear, so I don't know if that's a good idea. I think we need to just leave the background uniform, but it might be something to play with to make it look cool.

**assistant**: Yeah, a branded photo background sounds cool until a label washes out over a dark terminal shot — that's how you lose a trailer number at two in the morning. Uniform parchment is the safe play for anything with text on it. If you want to play with the branded look, test it on a screen that doesn't carry critical info — like a splash or idle state — and keep the working screens clean. What else you got?

**user**: So those buttons are just, okay so you see where it says training, documents, trip log, and qualifications? We never touch those. Some drivers do touch the documents because they need to, like if they break down or something like that, they might touch that. The training, we don't, we can't even use the training 'cause it doesn't work on this these tablets. The trip log, I've never touched that in three years, so I don't even know what that does. And then qualifications, what what is that? I don't even know what that is. I I don't need a button to tell me what my qualifications are. I've been doing this for thirty years, you know what I'm saying? So I don't I don't know what that is. But all those buttons, worthless buttons like that, taking up all that space, I almost would rather those be like a pop, a swing out, like it's a uh other uh button that when you tap it, all those other buttons swing out and it gives you more space on the screen. The things that need to be the largest is the HOS, that's the hours of service, that needs to be large 'cause that's what's the driver's going off of for his day. Um, and we have breaks and stuff, you see the little circles counting down. Uh, the drive smart, that's a safety thing, so the reason they got that there, we're not going to be able to make that any smaller, and if we can make it bigger, they would probably be happy. The tasks, that's another thing that is kinda stupid. Uh, it has to do with training. Um, sometimes it pops up, like uh, tasks can be if I'm um Oh what does the task pop up? Uh, like I haven't signed my logs for the day, so it'll tell me hey you you've got a task and it's but instead of it just giving like a a vague notion, it literally needs to pop up and say you need to sign your logs for January, you know, 7th through the 9th or some whatever, you know, relevant date, not generic crap that hey you got a task.

**assistant**: Collapsing the dead weight into a single Other swing-out is smart — training's broken anyway, trip log's a mystery, and qualifications is just noise for a thirty-year driver.

**user**: Okay, the sign out needs to be more prominent. Um, that's used like when we're swapping trucks and stuff. Um, and the vehicle, I I almost wish we could actually pull real data, like I'm on 61784 right now, that's a C and G truck. And it and I would really like vehicle and the truck number under my name, that to be one thing. There's no reason to have vehicles and literally listing the truck number up there, so that would be a button, and I would like it to uh be a relevant button of like this is a C and G truck, um, and it's a single screw. Those are two really important things to a truck driver, like if I'm being told to go drive 61784, I automatically already know um that that this truck is a C and G and it's a single axle. More than that, I'm going to want this data to float to the dashboard that I'm going to create for the dispatch. Because the dispatch needs to know that relevant data also. I think they already got it in some form, but their their their screens are all scattered around, like ours is. Did I lose ya?

**assistant**: Still here — sign-out bigger for truck swaps, and the vehicle line merged with the truck number into one button showing it's a C and G single-screw, with that same data floating up to the dispatch dashboard.

**user**: Uh, keep in mind, that's going to be dynamic. Um, you know, sometimes it's a twin screw and it's a diesel. Um, stuff like that. So that that data is going to be relevant to whatever truck you're actually getting into, and I think we can actually pull that from the S400 or from um Estee's actual, I don't I'm not even sure what the name of their software is, but we can get that.

**assistant**: Dynamic, yeah — whatever truck you climb into, the button shows its real config: twin screw, diesel, whatever it is.

**assistant**: Pulling it live from Estes' side means no stale info when you hop trucks. You still going, or is that the full list?

**user**: Uh, one more thing. Um, so most of our trailers are using a system where we can see where they are, they ping every once in a while, and it pops up that uh so we can find our trailers, right? Except it works sometimes, sometimes it doesn't. So what um along with that Starlink system, I want to see how feasible it is to use the current hardware that's already built into every single last trailer, I and see if we can actually figure out a way to hook that into uh Starlink. I think it's Qualcomm equipment, but I'm not sure.

**assistant**: Trailer tracking's flaky today, so wiring the Qualcomm gear already on every trailer into Starlink is worth a real feasibility pass.

**assistant**: That's the last of it from you — six items total, from parchment to the Starlink trailer hookup. The trailer hardware check is running now — I'll have something on whether that Qualcomm box can actually talk to Starlink. Anything else on your mind, or you want to start shaping the dispatch dashboard you mentioned?

**user**: No, uh, save all this stuff to a a new repo on GitHub, um, so we don't confuse projects.

**assistant**: Spinning up a fresh GitHub repo for all six items.

**assistant**: That ran long — trimming it down.

**user**: Okay, I'm in the uh I'm in the office. I'll talk to you later.

**assistant**: Talk soon — repo's going up now.
